_comment: Tier 2 benchmark corpus. The MESHES ARE NEVER COMMITTED — only this manifest is, so the
repository stays asset-free and a clone stays small. The harness skips Tier 2 with a warning
when the folder is absent, so CI stays green without it.
Override with the NATIVEREMESHER_CORPUS environment variable.
Only .obj files in the top level of that folder are picked up (see MeshCorpus.External).
Drop the files in with exactly the 'file' names below.
Tier 1 (procedural) needs none of this and always runs. Tier 2 exists because procedural
meshes are clean in ways real content is not: they have no scanner noise, no CAD
tessellation artefacts, no inconsistent normals, and no unhelpful topology. A remesher that
only ever sees Tier 1 will be tuned for a world that does not exist.

meshes.name: Stanford Bunny
meshes.why: The standard organic reference. Closed, moderate genus, well-behaved.

meshes.name: Stanford Armadillo
meshes.why: Organic with fine extremities — tests whether thin features survive coarsening.

meshes.name: Fandisk
meshes.why: THE hard-surface benchmark. Sharp creases and flat panels meeting at known angles. This is the mesh that shows whether feature detection is doing anything.

meshes.name: Rocker Arm
meshes.why: Mechanical part: fillets, holes, mixed curvature. Closer to real prop work than fandisk.

meshes.name: Photogrammetry scan (any)
meshes.why: Placeholder for a real scan. Dense, noisy, no clean features, possibly non-manifold. The photogrammetry profile is tuned against this and nothing else is a substitute.
